product_one_liner.value: Karbon is a cloud-based practice-management platform for accounting firms that brings client-management/CRM, email, tasks, invoicing, and payments together.
product_one_liner.notes: Karbon’s client-management page describes its cloud practice-management product for accounting firms and names CRM, email, task management, invoicing, and payments as integrated capabilities.

pricing_page.notes: The cited Karbon page is its public pricing/plans page for accounting firms.

named_customers.notes: named_customers: Karbon’s customer-story pages identify System Six and BKL as customers. | named_customers.0: The Karbon customer-story page is titled “System Six eradicated chaos with Karbon.” | named_customers.1: The Karbon customer-story page is titled “How BKL uses Karbon to save 4 days per month.”

employee_band.notes: The LinkedIn company profile places Karbon in the 201–500 employee size band.

hq_location.notes: hq_city: The GLEIF record lists San Francisco as the headquarters city for Karbon, Inc. | hq_country: The GLEIF record for Karbon, Inc. identifies its headquarters country as the United States.

founded_year.notes: Karbon’s LinkedIn company profile states it was founded in 2014.

eng_blog.notes: Karbon describes its company blog as covering customers and the startup journey. The reviewed Magazine material surfaced one engineering-authored post about its product-development shipathon, but not two qualifying engineering/technical posts; this supports a negative, though the site’s full index is not fully rendered.

public_docs.notes: Karbon’s public Developer Center links API documentation, guides, issues, and release notes, satisfying the public documentation/developer portal criterion.

ai_ml_roles_open.notes: Karbon’s live job posting is titled AI Operations Lead and includes an Apply control, so an AI-titled role is open.

model_provider.notes: Karbon’s AI feature page explicitly names Azure OpenAI Service as the service powering Karbon AI.

compliance_certs.notes: compliance_certs: Karbon’s security page says its web application is SOC 2 Type 2 certified. The same page says it is not independently ISO 27001 certified, so ISO 27001 is excluded; the listed public certification is SOC 2 Type II. | compliance_certs.0: The Karbon security page explicitly names SOC 2 Type 2 certification.

last_funding.notes: funding_stage: PitchBook labels the latest financing as Later Stage VC, Series B. | funding_date: PitchBook dates Karbon’s latest financing to July 17, 2024, which formats as 2024-07. | funding_amount_usd: PitchBook reports the most recent financing as a $10.5 million Series B round dated July 17, 2024; the requested amount in USD is 10,500,000.

raised_18mo.notes: PitchBook gives July 17, 2024 as the latest financing date, before the 18-month window beginning May 9, 2025, so the answer is false.

hiring_sdr_ae.notes: Karbon’s Greenhouse listing shows an Account Executive, SMB opening with an Apply action; account executives qualify under the question’s rule.

launched_6mo.notes: Karbon’s first-party release notes dated October 6, 2026 say Engagements became available to all customers starting that day, a major feature launch inside the six-month window.

leadership_change_12mo.notes: Karbon announced on October 6, 2026 that Stuart Totman was promoted to Chief Technology Officer, a C-level leadership change within the requested 12-month window.

crm_stack_signal.notes: crm_stack_signal: Karbon’s account-executive job posting instructs staff to maintain information in Salesforce/Gong, naming both systems. | crm_stack_signal.0: The job posting expressly names Salesforce. | crm_stack_signal.1: The job posting expressly names Gong.
